summary: Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff was a scholar in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Schulpforta, Bonn, and Berlin under Johannes Schmidt, Moriz Haupt, and Otto Jahn. He held professorships at Greifswald (1876-1883), Göttingen (1883-1897), and Berlin (1897-1921).

Ulrike Roesler is a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Münster. She taught Indian and Tibetan studies at Freiburg and Marburg, and became Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford.

Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Indologist. She studied at Mount Carmel College, Bangalore Institute of Legal Studies, Banaras Hindu University, Miranda House, and the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti. She served as an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

Umakant Premanand Shah was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, as deputy director in 1954 and head of the Ramayana Project in 1965, and was director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1955-1975).

Umesha Mishra was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He worked at the University of Allahabad (1923-1958), co-founded the Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha in 1943, and served as Director of the Mithila Institute from ~1951 to 1958.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana is a scholar of Indology who studied at Bharathiar University and the University of Amsterdam. He held positions at FRLHT, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama as a visiting fellow and visiting associate professor.

Unrai Wogihara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Jōdo Shūgaku Honkō and Strasbourg under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Shukyo University, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Taisho University.
Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded Juzen-kai in 1884, as well as Kairitsu Gakkō and Juuzen Hokutsu.

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London and served as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem works in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at MSUE, Eötvös Loránd University, and UC Berkeley (PhD). She held positions at MSUE, Yonsei, Berkeley, the National University of Mongolia, and IUPUI as Fehnel Chair in 2019.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley, where she served as an Art History lecturer, and became Associate Professor at the National University of Mongolia.

Urs App works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Fribourg, Kyoto, and Temple under Seizan Yanagida and Victor H. Mair, and served as Associate Director at the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism at Hanazono University (1989-1999).

Usharbudh Arya was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of London from around 1960 to 1967 and held a post at the University of Minnesota from approximately 1967 to 1973.

Ute Hüsken is an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Göttingen under Heinz Bechert and Heidelberg. Her appointments include Göttingen, Professor at the University of Oslo (2007-2017), and Professor at the South Asia Institute, Heidelberg (2017).

Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna (1965-1972). He served as a university lecturer in Indology at the University of Vienna starting in 1969 and completed research at the University of Madras (1972-1974).

V. Raghavan was an Indologist who studied at Presidency College and the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served in the Sanskrit Department at the University of Madras (1934-1968) and as Adviser at Adyar Library (~1969-1979).

V. S. Sukthankar was an Indologist who studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1915-1919) and became General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI in 1925.

V. Venkatachalam was an Indologist who studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram universities. He taught at Vikram University (1974-1985), directed the Scindia Oriental Research Institute, and was Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University.

V. Venkayya was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras, and served as acting Government Epigraphist of Madras (~1903-1908) and for the Archaeological Survey of India (1905).

V. W. Paranjpe was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Superintendent of the Publication Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1927) and held the title of Professor Emeritus at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
